title: Document and harden format!("{cap}") for CapabilityEnable string dispatch
description: mod.rs line 474 converts a typed CapabilityEnable value to a string via format!("{cap}") then passes the string to handle_enable() for case-insensitive comparison. This is fragile in two ways: (1) if the imap-types Display impl for CapabilityEnable changes output format (e.g. adds prefix, changes case rules, or the variant is renamed), the comparison in handle_enable silently stops matching and ENABLE IMAP4rev2 becomes a silent no-op with no test failure; (2) the pattern is invisible — a reader sees format!("{cap}") and cannot tell this is intentional dispatch-by-display rather than a diagnostic string. There is no comment explaining why a typed match arm is not used instead. The root cause is the same upstream gap as x7ki.3 (no typed Capability::Imap4Rev2 / CapabilityEnable::Imap4Rev2 variant), but the fragility is distinct: the conversion from typed cap to string is the load-bearing step and it silently degrades. Fix: add a comment above the format! call explaining the workaround and its failure mode. When upstream ships a typed CapabilityEnable::Imap4Rev2 variant, replace the format!/handle_enable string dispatch with a typed match arm so the compiler enforces correctness.
